ToolHive (thv) is a lightweight, secure, and fast manager for MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers.
It is written in Go and has extensive test coverage—including input validation—to ensure reliability and security.

Under the hood, ToolHive acts as a very thin client for the Docker/Podman/Colima Unix socket API.
This design choice allows it to remain both efficient and lightweight while still providing powerful,
container-based isolation for running MCP servers.

Usage:
  thv [flags]
  thv [command]

Available Commands:
  ai-plugin   Manage AI-tool plugins
  build       Build a container for an MCP server without running it
  client      Manage MCP clients
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  config      Manage application configuration
  export      Export a workload's run configuration to a file
  group       Manage logical groupings of MCP servers
  help        Help about any command
  inspector   Launches the MCP Inspector UI and connects it to the specified MCP server
  list        List running MCP servers
  llm         Manage LLM gateway authentication
  logs        Output the logs of an MCP server or manage log files
  mcp         Interact with MCP servers for debugging
  proxy       Create a transparent proxy for an MCP server with authentication support
  registry    Manage MCP server registry
  rm          Remove one or more MCP servers
  run         Run an MCP server
  runtime     Commands related to the container runtime
  search      Search for MCP servers
  secret      Manage secrets
  serve       Start the ToolHive API server
  skill       Manage skills
  start       Start (resume) a tooling server
  status      Show detailed status of an MCP server
  stop        Stop one or more MCP servers
  tui         Open the interactive TUI dashboard (experimental)
  upgrade     Manage upgrades for MCP server workloads
  version     Show the version of ToolHive
  vmcp        Run and manage a Virtual MCP Server locally

Flags:
      --debug   Enable debug mode
  -h, --help    help for thv

Use "thv [command] --help" for more information about a command.
